Alive

A brain that grows its own cells in the cloud, every hour, with its owner's PC off: its arms write candidate cells, a locked judge grades each one on held-out questions, and only the survivors join it.

Generation 6 ran 7 hours before this page was built: 6 of 6 candidate cells survived the locked judge, and 144 cells are alive.

The organism by itself

No model runs in this loop. Each era the organism absorbs open data, opens tasks from it, grows cells for every task by composing its own primitives, tries changes to its own engine, measures itself and commits them, on whichever body is beating. Every number below is read from the committed file named under it when this page was built; a file not written yet reads "not yet".

Not working yet: only 52 of 393 tasks are mastered; 132 of 393 tasks have a colony at all; the colonies answer 3860 of 5987 held-out rows right (0.6447).
